verdict.summary: Creating your own OAuth app and connecting your own account is quick. Getting the app listed in the Klaviyo App Marketplace is the hard part: it needs a formal review, a security review, a testing package, a demo video, listing assets, and at least 5 real customer installs first. Klaviyo publishes no review timeline.
verdict.hands_on_effort: Own-account setup: under an hour. Full marketplace submission package: multi-day work (not quantified in the findings).
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Minutes after you have the client ID and client secret and a role that can create apps.
verdict.approval_wait: No published duration. Klaviyo says it will follow up by email. Not verified.

gates.name: Own app, own account (development use)
gates.unlocks: You create the OAuth app, add scopes and redirect URLs, and connect your own Klaviyo account through the OAuth flow.
limits: Only owner, admin, and manager roles can create OAuth apps.
The client secret is shown once. You can generate a new one later from the UI.
Access tokens last about 1 hour (subject to change). Use the expires_in value from the token response.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes, once you have an owner, admin, or manager role in the Klaviyo account.

gates.name: Unreviewed app, invited customers and testers
gates.unlocks: Customers and testers can install and use the app before Klaviyo reviews it. Installs show an OAuth warning that the app has not been reviewed by Klaviyo. Reaching Gate 2 for real customers requires the OAuth flow to be working, and the 5-install threshold is a submission prerequisite.
limits: Customers see an OAuth installation warning until the app is approved.
No install cap for unreviewed apps was published.
Test accounts and developer or company-owned accounts do not count toward the 5-install submission threshold.
Testing instructions must be a Google Doc with Commenter access. Public documentation links are not accepted.
Credentials must not be sent in the submission or by email.
gates.time_to_reach: Days to weeks, depending on how fast you can get installs from customers and testers. Not measured in the findings.

gates.name: Marketplace listing (public discovery)
gates.unlocks: Approval removes the install warning and makes the app discoverable in the Klaviyo App Marketplace.
limits: Listing is optional, but requires a formal review.
Klaviyo runs a technical and security review. Apps must pass the security review before listing.
Rejected apps get detailed reasons and can be resubmitted.
Apps still using private-key authentication are delisted. Published partners must use OAuth.
gates.time_to_reach: Unknown. No review duration is published. Klaviyo may decline to list an app for any reason.

steps.title: Confirm your role in the Klaviyo account
steps.detail: Only owner, admin, and manager roles can create OAuth apps. If you do not have one of these roles, ask an account owner to create the app or to change your role before you continue.
gotchas: A developer with a lower role will not see the option to create the app.

steps.title: Create the app in Manage apps
steps.detail: Open the Manage apps page. Select Create app, then enter a name for the app. Klaviyo's guide names this as the step that creates the OAuth app.
gotchas: Name the app for the integration, not for a single customer. The name carries into the listing if you submit later.

steps.title: Save the client ID and client secret
steps.detail: On the Set up OAuth screen, copy the client ID and the client secret. The secret cannot be viewed again. If you lose it, generate a new one from the UI.
gotchas: Store the secret in a secrets store. Do not hardcode it in application code.
Once you lose the secret, the only fix is to generate a new one, which may invalidate the old one. Confirm the behaviour in the UI before relying on it.

steps.title: Set scopes to the minimum your integration calls
steps.detail: Agent task: list every Klaviyo endpoint the integration calls, then look up each endpoint's API reference page for its required scopes. Draft a space-separated scope list that includes only those scopes, and keep accounts:read in the list. Do not paste the full Composio default list. Give the developer the final list to enter in the app's scope field.

values.label: Scope field format
values.value: Space-separated list. accounts:read is required and must stay in the list.

values.label: Composio default list
values.value: Do not use. It includes many write scopes (for example campaigns:write, flows:write) that most integrations do not need.

gotchas: Requesting scopes the app does not use is a rejection cause.
Klaviyo's own 'Don't' example warns against requesting all available scopes.

steps.title: Enter scopes and redirect URI, then save
steps.detail: Paste the trimmed scope list into the app's scope field. In the redirect URL field, paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config. For more than one redirect URL, separate entries with a space, tab, or new line. Click Save.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

values.label: Scope field
values.value: Trimmed list from the previous step; accounts:read included

gotchas: The redirect_uri in the authorization request must match one allowlisted entry exactly, including scheme, path, and trailing slash.
Do not add the Composio default redirect URI from memory. Use the value shown in your Composio auth config.

steps.title: Connect your own account through Composio
steps.detail: Enter the client ID and client secret in your Composio auth config for Klaviyo. Start a connection from Composio and sign in with your own Klaviyo account. The authorization request must include PKCE (code_challenge_method=S256), and each request needs a new verifier and challenge.
gotchas: The authorization code expires 5 minutes after issue. The callback must exchange it promptly.
Token traffic must go to a.klaviyo.com. Klaviyo began blocking OAuth token traffic sent through www.klaviyo.com on March 31, 2025.

steps.title: Test token refresh and error handling
steps.detail: Agent task: run a test that uses the access token, waits for expiry or forces a refresh, and confirms the new token works. Check that the code reads expires_in from the token response. Confirm the code handles 401 authentication_failed by refreshing, and handles invalid_grant by asking the customer to reauthorize. Keep refresh calls under 10 per minute per token.

values.label: Refresh limit
values.value: 10 refresh calls per minute per refresh token

gotchas: Access tokens can be up to 4,096 characters. Refresh tokens can be up to 512. Storage columns must allow for that length.
Refresh tokens stay valid until the customer uninstalls the app, unless unused for 90 days. An unused token is revoked.

steps.title: Build the install flow and settings page
steps.detail: Agent task: draft the installation URL and confirm it sends a logged-in user straight into the OAuth flow with all required query parameters. The install flow must work from klaviyo.com and from its subdomains. Add a settings URL that points to a Klaviyo-specific integration settings page. Handle install, uninstall, and error flows. Developer task: review the flow end to end in a browser.

values.label: Settings URL
values.value: A Klaviyo-specific integration settings page on your site

values.label: Installation URL
values.value: Must require login first, then go straight to OAuth. No intermediate integrations page or extra redirects.

gotchas: An install link that routes through an integrations page or extra screens is a submission problem.
Test the install from a klaviyo.com subdomain as well as klaviyo.com.

steps.title: Get 5 real customer installs with live API activity
steps.detail: Share the installation URL with real customers. Installing the app does not require the app to be listed. The 5 installs must show production API activity. Developer accounts, test accounts, and company-linked accounts do not count.

values.label: Minimum installs for submission
values.value: 5 active customer installs with live API activity

gotchas: Test accounts do not qualify.
This is a submission prerequisite. It is not a limit on installs.

steps.title: Complete the one-time company registration and agreements
steps.detail: Complete the one-time integration registration form for your company. Provide the company name, description, website URL, and at least one contact email for the review team. Accept the Technology Partner Agreement, Klaviyo's Acceptable Use Policy, and the API Terms of Use. Give accurate company and app information.
gotchas: Your company only needs to submit this form once.
The form is a legal acceptance. Only someone authorised to bind the company should complete it.

steps.title: Draft the listing content and assets
steps.detail: Agent task: draft the developer name (30 characters or fewer), category, short description (75 characters), full description (300 characters), 2 to 6 key features (title 65 characters, description 225 characters), and at least one user guide (titles 100 characters, descriptions 200). Include a privacy policy URL, support contact, pricing info URL, and terms of service link. Do not use the words preferred, recommended, top performing, or best. Developer task: prepare an SVG logo (48 by 48 pixels, no scripting) and a gallery of 4 to 8 images or a cover image, plus an optional video.

values.label: Gallery
values.value: Cover image, or 4 to 8 images, with optional video

gotchas: The website must show current visuals and a demo video.
The docs do not say whether domain verification is required. Confirm with Klaviyo.

steps.title: Complete the security standards and security form
steps.detail: Confirm your app meets the security standards: TLS 1.2 or higher in transit, OAuth tokens encrypted at rest with an algorithm such as AES-256, MFA on systems that handle data, expiring tokens the app rejects once expired, role-based access, secrets store for client credentials, and audit logs kept for at least 365 days. Fill out the security form for this app with true and complete information.
gotchas: A security form is required for each unique app your company submits.
Critical or high-severity library vulnerabilities have fix windows of 3 and 7 days.

steps.title: Prepare the testing package
steps.detail: Agent task: adapt Klaviyo's testing-instructions template into a Google Doc. Include the list of endpoints with their use cases and scopes, an architecture diagram of data flow, and steps for the reviewer to test the OAuth flow end to end. Include a test account path for the reviewer, including paid-app access if relevant. Share the doc with Commenter access. Developer task: record a demo video and add it to the doc.

values.label: Document type
values.value: Google Doc, Commenter access, adapted from Klaviyo's testing template

gotchas: Do not send account credentials in the submission or by email. Invite the reviewer's address or send a password reset.
Links to public documentation are not accepted.

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.detail: Go to Integrations > Developers > Manage apps. Open your app and click Review submission. Confirm the scope list, redirect URLs, listing content, security form, and testing package are final before you submit.

values.label: Menu path
values.value: Integrations > Developers > Manage apps > [your app] > Review submission

gotchas: Submitting for review is optional. Installs can continue without it, but the install warning stays on.
Scopes you do not use will cause rejection. Recheck the scope list before submitting.

steps.title: Wait for the review decision
steps.detail: Klaviyo's team runs a technical and security review. Klaviyo will follow up by email on approval or required changes. If rejected, you get detailed reasons. Fix them and resubmit.
gotchas: No review duration is published.
Klaviyo may decline to list an app for any reason, even after review.

requirements.item: Owner, admin, or manager role in the Klaviyo account
requirements.detail: Needed to create an OAuth app. Other roles cannot create one.
Use code_challenge_method=S256 with a new code_verifier and code_challenge per request. Required for public and confidential clients.
Code exchange and refresh go to a.klaviyo.com with a Basic Authorization header and a form-encoded body. Token traffic through www.klaviyo.com is blocked.
The redirect_uri must exactly match one allowlisted entry. Multiple entries are separated by space, tab, or new line.
Request only scopes the app uses. accounts:read is required by default and must stay in the list. Over-requesting causes rejection.
The app must install from klaviyo.com and any of its subdomains.

requirements.item: Install flow requires login first and goes straight to OAuth
requirements.detail: No intermediate integrations page or extra redirects. All required query parameters included.

requirements.item: Settings URL and full install, uninstall, and error handling
requirements.detail: Settings URL points to a Klaviyo-specific integration settings page. The OAuth flow handles install, uninstall, and error cases.

requirements.item: 5 active customer installs with live API activity
requirements.detail: Required before submission. Test accounts, developer accounts, and company-linked accounts do not count.

requirements.item: One-time company registration form and agreements
requirements.detail: Accept the Technology Partner Agreement, Acceptable Use Policy, and API Terms of Use. Company only needs to submit once.

Developer name 30 characters or fewer; short description 75 characters; full description 300; 2-6 key features; at least one user guide; SVG logo 48x48 with no scripting; gallery of 4-8 images or a cover image; website, privacy policy, support contact, pricing URL.
Do not describe the app as Klaviyo's preferred, recommended, top performing, or best partner without written approval.

TLS 1.2+ in transit; OAuth tokens encrypted at rest (for example AES-256); MFA for systems that handle data; expiring tokens rejected after expiry; role-based access; secrets store for client credentials; audit logs kept 365 days; security form per app.
Google Doc with Commenter access, endpoint list with scopes, data-flow architecture diagram, demo recording, and reviewer test path. No credentials in the submission or email.
Klaviyo's security team reviews the security form and the app. Apps must pass before listing.

requirements.item: Rate limits per installed app instance
requirements.detail: OAuth apps get their own quota per installed app per account. Endpoint limits are tiered (XS to XL) with burst (1-second) and steady (1-minute) windows. Exceeding a limit returns HTTP 429.
Use exponential backoff and respect Retry-After. Immediate retries get another 429.

scopes.effect: Required by default. Must stay in the list. No separate review tier was found in the docs.

scopes.scope: campaigns:write, flows:write, profiles:write, and other *:write scopes in the Composio default list
scopes.effect: Include only if the integration actually calls the endpoint. Unused write scopes are a rejection cause.

scopes.scope: All scopes in the Composio default list
scopes.effect: Do not request all of them. Klaviyo lists requesting all scopes as a 'Don't' example. The docs describe no scope tiers that trigger extra review.

blockers.symptom: You cannot find the option to create an OAuth app in Klaviyo.
blockers.cause: Your account role is not owner, admin, or manager.
blockers.fix: Ask an owner or admin to create the app, or to change your role to admin or manager.

blockers.symptom: Submission is rejected for requesting scopes the app does not need.
blockers.cause: The scope list was copied from the Composio default, which includes many write and unused scopes.
blockers.fix: List every endpoint the integration calls, look up its scopes on the API reference, keep accounts:read, remove the rest, and resubmit.

blockers.symptom: The authorization request fails because the redirect URI does not match.
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri in the request is not exactly one of the allowlisted entries on the app.
blockers.fix: Copy the callback URL from your Composio auth config into the redirect URL field exactly, then retry.

blockers.symptom: Token exchange or refresh fails after Klaviyo changed the endpoint.
blockers.cause: Token traffic was sent through www.klaviyo.com. Klaviyo blocks OAuth token traffic there from March 31, 2025.
blockers.fix: Send code exchange and refresh requests to https://a.klaviyo.com/oauth/token.

blockers.symptom: Authorization code exchange fails with an expired code.
blockers.cause: The authorization code expires 5 minutes after issue, and the callback took longer than that.
blockers.fix: Exchange the code immediately in the callback. Do not queue it.

blockers.symptom: Refresh returns invalid_grant (400-02). The customer's connection stops working.
blockers.cause: The customer uninstalled the app, or the app called /oauth/revoke.
blockers.fix: Ask the customer to reauthorize the app. Store the new tokens.

blockers.symptom: Refresh returns 400-03 (refresh token expired due to inactivity).
blockers.cause: The refresh token was unused for more than 90 days.
blockers.fix: The customer must reauthorize. Refresh tokens must be used at least every 90 days to avoid this.

blockers.symptom: Refresh returns invalid_grant with 'Refresh token has been revoked' while the customer is still connected and within 90 days (community report).
blockers.cause: Unverified. One community post reports this during development. Klaviyo's docs do not list this as a cause.
blockers.fix: Ask the customer to reauthorize. If this recurs, contact Klaviyo support with the error details.

blockers.cause: The integration is suspended, or the company that owns the OAuth client is deactivated.
blockers.fix: For 400-99, contact Klaviyo support. For 400-98, check the status of the integration in your Klaviyo account.
blockers.contact: Klaviyo support (channel not specified in the findings)

blockers.cause: More than 10 refresh calls per minute on one refresh token.
blockers.fix: Cache the access token and refresh only when it is near expiry. Use exponential backoff and respect Retry-After.

blockers.symptom: Submission cannot be started or is blocked before review.
blockers.cause: Fewer than 5 customer installs have live production API activity. Test and developer accounts do not count.
blockers.fix: Get 5 real customer installs with live API activity, then submit.

blockers.symptom: Submission is rejected after security review.
blockers.cause: The app or security form does not meet Klaviyo's security standards, such as token encryption, MFA, or log retention.
blockers.fix: Read the detailed rejection reasons, fix the gaps, update the security form, and resubmit.

blockers.symptom: Reviewer cannot test the app, or the submission is returned.
blockers.cause: Testing instructions link to public docs, or credentials were sent in the submission or by email.
blockers.fix: Use a Google Doc with Commenter access, adapted from the testing template. Invite the reviewer's address or send a password reset instead of sharing credentials.

composio.note: Composio has a Klaviyo OAuth2 auth config but no managed OAuth app (managed_oauth_available is false). You must register your own Klaviyo OAuth app and enter its client ID and client secret in Composio. Do not use Composio's default scope list as-is: it is broad and includes write scopes. Trim it to the scopes your integration calls before submission. Confirm the callback URL Composio expects before adding it to the Klaviyo allowlist.
